summary: Learn QGIS, Sentinel-2 and forest-condition mapping through practical exercises. Explore the five-day training outline and course content.
lede: Forest health monitoring combines satellite imagery, GIS layers and field observations to assess forest condition and change. For forestry, conservation and land-management professionals, the course covers preparing forest data in QGIS, interpreting NDVI and disturbance signals, and checking map accuracy. Learners compare observations over time and produce maps and priority lists to guide field verification and management attention.
audienceIntro: This foundation-level course is for people who collect, maintain, interpret, or act on spatial evidence about forest condition. It suits professionals who need a repeatable way to connect imagery, field observations, and management priorities without programming.
audience: Forest Planning Officers using spatial evidence
prerequisites: No prior GIS or remote-sensing experience is required. Basic computer use and familiarity with forestry, conservation, or environmental work will help you connect the exercises to your role. Programming is not required.
